age.evidence: Adult male and timed-pregnant Sprague-Dawley rats were used for this study.

sex.evidence: the protective effect of psilocybin was examined in male animals in this study.

dosing.evidence: psilocybin (100 µM x 20 µL, n = 7) or vehicle (saline, 20 µl, n = 7) was administered intracerebroventricularly (i.c.v.) at 15 min before the right middle cerebral artery occlusion... In the post-treatment group, psilocybin (1 mg/kg/day, n = 7) or vehicle ( n = 6) was administered i.p. from day 3 to day 7.

enrichment_housing.evidence: All experiment procedures, including housing and husbandry conditions, environmental enrichment, animal care/monitoring, and humane endpoints, were carried out in accordance with the National Institutes of Health Guidelines (mentions enrichment as a procedure but does not specify whether home cage enrichment was provided).

assays.assay_description: Rats suspended 20 cm above the table by the tail; frequency of initial turning of the head or upper body contralateral to the ischemic side counted across 20 consecutive trials. Conducted on D2 (i.c.v. pretreatment cohort) and D9 (i.p. post-treatment cohort).

application_type.evidence: psilocybin... administered intracerebroventricularly (i.c.v.) at 15 min before MCAo... psilocybin (1 mg/kg/day) was administered i.p. from day 3 to day 7.

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were examined for lateral movements/turning when their bodies were suspended 20 cm above the testing table by lifting their tails.

food_restriction.evidence: Standard short test; food not in apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard short test; water not in apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: Behavioral tests were conducted two days (or D2) after the MCAo [pretreatment, ~48h after i.c.v. dose]; Behavioral tests were conducted on day 9 [post-treatment, 48h after last i.p. dose on day 7].

sample_size.evidence: A total of 18 adult rats were used for this analysis... n=7 per group... psilocybin (1 mg/kg/d, n=7) or vehicle (n=6)... Four non-stroke rats were used as naive controls.

outcomes.summary: Stroke increased body asymmetry; both pre- (i.c.v.) and post-treatment (i.p.) psilocybin significantly reduced body asymmetry. ANA12 antagonized the psilocybin-mediated improvement.
outcomes.statistics: Pretreatment: p=0.002 (stroke+veh vs. stroke+Psi); ANA12 antagonism p=0.012; Post-treatment: p=0.026 (one-way ANOVA + NK test).
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin significantly reduced... body asymmetry (Fig. 3-B2, p = 0.002, stroke + veh vs. stroke + Psi)... B2: body asymmetry, p = 0.026.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Frequency of contralateral turning counted in 20 trials (single measure).

B4_ethological.evidence: Forced postural response, not natural behaviour.

D1_continuity.evidence: Tests on D2 (pretreatment cohort) and D9 (post-treatment cohort).

D3_recording_days.evidence: Within each cohort, asymmetry was tested on a single day (D2 for pretreatment, D9 for post-treatment).

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-stroke baseline test reported for the same assay.

D5_followup.evidence: In post-treatment cohort, behavioral tests were conducted on day 9, 48h after the last i.p. dose on day 7.

assays.assay_description: Postural reflex test: rats suspended 20-30 cm above the testing table and scored 0-3 on forelimb extension, lateral resistance, and twisting. Conducted on D2 (pretreatment) and D9 (post-treatment).

application_type.evidence: psilocybin... administered intracerebroventricularly (i.c.v.)... or i.p. from day 3 to day 7.

setup_restrain.evidence: rats were examined for the degree of abnormal posture when suspended by 20-30 cm above the testing table.

time_to_assay.evidence: Tests on D2 after MCAo (pretreatment) and D9 (after i.p. dosing days 3-7).

sample_size.evidence: n = 7 per group; vehicle post-treatment n = 6; 4 non-stroke controls.

outcomes.summary: Stroke increased Bederson's neurological score; both pre- and post-treatment psilocybin significantly reduced the score. ANA12 antagonized this protection.
outcomes.statistics: Pretreatment: p=0.011; ANA12 antagonism p=0.012; Post-treatment: p=0.024 (one-way ANOVA + NK test).
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin significantly reduced the Bederson's neurological score (Fig. 3-B1, p = 0.011)... Psi post-treatment significantly reduced (B1) Bederson's neurological score (p = 0.024).

D1_continuity.evidence: Within each cohort, the test was performed once (D2 for pretreatment, D9 for post-treatment).

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-stroke baseline reported for this assay.

D5_followup.evidence: In post-treatment cohort, test on day 9 = 48h after last dose on day 7.

assays.assay_description: Rats individually placed in a 3D infrared behavior chamber (42 × 42 × 21 cm) for 60 min; horizontal activity (HACTV), total distance traveled (TOTDIST), movement number (MOVNO), and movement time (MOVTIME) recorded via Accuscan beam-break system. Tested on D2 (pretreatment) and D9 (post-treatment).

application_type.evidence: psilocybin... administered i.c.v. before MCAo... or i.p. from day 3 to day 7.

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were individually placed in a 3D infrared behavior chamber (42 × 42 × 21 cm) for 60 min.

time_to_assay.evidence: Locomotor activity was monitored for one hour on day 2... [post-treatment] Behavioral tests were conducted on day 9.

sample_size.evidence: n = 7 per group; vehicle post-treatment n = 6; 4 non-stroke controls.

outcomes.summary: Stroke significantly reduced locomotor activity (HACTV, TOTDIST, MOVNO, MOVTIME). Both pre- and post-treatment with psilocybin increased locomotor activity; ANA12 antagonized the pretreatment effect.
outcomes.statistics: Pretreatment: HACTV p=0.039, TOTDIST p=0.032, MOVNO p=0.0284, MOVTIME p=0.056; ANA12 antagonism HACTV p=0.009, TOTDIST p=0.018. Post-treatment: HACTV p=0.009, TOTDIST p=0.009, MOVNO p=0.022, MOVTIME p=0.02 (one-way ANOVA + NK test).
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin increased horizontal activity (HACTV, p = 0.039), total distance traveled (TOTODIST, p = 0.032), and movement number (MOVNO, p = 0.0284)... [post-treatment] C1: horizontal activity p = 0.009; C2: total distance traveled, p = 0.009; C3: movement number, p = 0.022; C4: movement time, p = 0.02.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Four parameters: HACTV, TOTDIST, MOVNO, MOVTIME.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Totals reported across 60-min session; no within-session time-course analysis described.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Accuscan infrared beam-break system - not behavioural classification.

E8_food_water.evidence: Standard short locomotor test, no food/water.

D1_continuity.evidence: Within each cohort, locomotor activity recorded once (D2 or D9).

D2_session_duration.evidence: Rats were individually placed in a 3D infrared behavior chamber (42 × 42 × 21 cm) for 60 min.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline session for this assay reported.

D5_followup.evidence: Post-treatment cohort tested on day 9, 48h after last i.p. dose on day 7.

judge_notes: Excluded in vitro primary cortical neuronal culture experiments (MAP2 immunocytochemistry, ANA12 in vitro) - these are ex vivo molecular endpoints, not rodent behaviour.
Excluded TTC infarct measurement and qRT-PCR (MAP2, synaptophysin, IBA1, BDNF) - histological/molecular endpoints.
Kept the Elevated Body Asymmetry Test and Bederson's Neurological Test as separate assays (different apparatus parameters, different scored constructs) consistent with both candidate models.
Merged pre- and post-treatment cohorts into single assay entries per paradigm (same behaviour, same apparatus; only manipulation/timing differs), per rubric decision rule.
B1 for asymmetry and Bederson scored 0 (single measure each), correcting glm's score of 1; locomotor scored 2 (4 measures).

D3 set to 1 (single recording day per cohort) for each behavioural assay, since each cohort experienced the test only once; rubric specifies counting days that THIS assay was administered, not all study days.
D5 set to Yes for all three assays because the post-treatment cohort was tested on day 9 (>=24 h after last dose on day 7).
DOI not present in extracted markdown; left null.

Housing enrichment scored not_reported (low confidence): the paper mentions enrichment as a procedural domain governed by NIH guidelines but does not explicitly describe enrichment items in home cages.
